event: Callum wakes on his cot in the warehouse to the hum of three constructs that ran all night.
He greets Pip, the gold cursor familiar on his shoulder, which has never once answered.
The overnight report: 8 hours 2 minutes on three threads, 1,247 Essence, a 2.04x yield multiplier.
He logs 1,247 in his notebook under 1,198 and 1,142, and draws the curve bending upward.
The Refinery is the bottleneck at 87.3%; he plans to batch its queue in the 2 AM spawn lull.
He stands and looks over the warehouse, a stripped stamping plant sixty feet by a hundred.
The Mk.IV Grinder by the east wall fights Level 8-10 mobs in the Rustbelt Flats through a relay.
He checks its anchors: 45 Flux an hour, and a hairline crack in the relay crystal to replace.
The Scrap Collector crawls the ruins to the north, stripping wire and metal for the Refinery.
The Refinery in the middle of the floor turns scrap into Flux Capacitor parts and refined alloy.
He activates Loop Sight: gold, green and blue threads spin between the three constructs.
On the west workbench the Enhancement Construct sits sixty percent built, short of Bloom Crystal.
He pictures the loop closing: upgrades fed back to every construct, output compounding.
"Eight Bloom Crystal fragments," he tells Pip. Pip blinks. The Exchange it is.
He walks twenty minutes through the manufacturing corridor, the air smelling of Flux smoke.
Guild teams jog to the gate and gatherers haul carts; nobody looks at the thin man in coveralls.
The Exchange opens up in the old Eastern Market, guild banners hung from its iron beams.
Traders cry Residuum at three hundred Gold a unit, pre-charged Flux cores, and potions.
At the botanical stall a wiry vendor sizes him up and asks fifty Gold a fragment for Bloom Crystal.
He has about 1,600 Gold, with 400 owed to the Barrier next week and 200 kept as a buffer.
He offers forty, citing the thorn elementals' seventy-two-hour cycle; she settles on forty-five.
He pays 360 Gold for eight fragments and winces at the balance.

event: The fragments sit warm and heavy in his satchel: enough to close the loop, if the math holds.
Two Iron Vanguard men by a pillar talk of a Residuum surcharge on unaffiliated players.
Twenty percent on top, the armored one tells Henley: Morrison wants everyone in his guild.
They move on; Callum, unaffiliated, works out 80 Gold more a week, delaying his construct.
He files it as a constraint, but sees plainly that Drake Morrison is squeezing the unaffiliated.
Near the north exit the Broker, whose real name nobody knows, moves through the crowd.
A vendor straightens, Vanguard members nod, and a guild leader steps out of the Broker's way.
Everyone defers, from respect or dependency, Callum notes, and moves on.
On the way home he passes the Grind Pits, walled arenas where active players spar.
A crowd rings the central arena, and the sound inside is fast and precise as a sewing machine.
A wiry woman of about twenty with a one-handed sword faces three higher-level sparring partners.
She steps into the shieldbearer's charge: a Critical Hit for 412 damage.
She slips the dual-wielder's cross-slash and cuts his forearm for 278 damage and a bleed.
She cuts a Flux bolt out of the air, then ripostes the staff-wielder for a 589-damage crit.
Eleven seconds, three opponents down. The crowd erupts; Callum runs numbers.
PER in the fifties or sixties, a Duelist or Sword Saint, about 116 damage a second, he reckons.
Extraordinary, he judges, and linear: her growth adds and never compounds. She has a ceiling.
She takes the crowd's praise impatiently; he walks home and thinks of DPS curves, not of her.
Back in the warehouse he sets the Bloom Crystal satchel beside the Enhancement Construct.
A notification: the Grinder's combat pattern has reached 100 iterations.
The reward is an Iteration Token, an upgrade for any of his three constructs.
He applies it to the Grinder, first link in the chain: attack efficiency 94.2% to 97.2%.
Three percent is a rounding error to anyone else; compounded over a hundred cycles it is not.
He writes the new overnight projection, 1,284 Essence, and circles the 37 twice.
He allows himself a small smile; Pip blinks once, slow and warm.
He tells Pip the Enhancement Construct starts tomorrow, the loop closed by week's end, if it holds.
Lying on the cot, he watches the three threads of light play over the corrugated ceiling.
He thinks of the woman with the sword, of the surcharge, of the Substrate humming beneath it all.
Nobody is watching yet. He lets the constructs hum him to sleep.
